answer: Each payout claim goes before a jury drawn at random from the grove of agents, which no operator can predict. The claimant must attach a kernel: a proof that its funding trail differs from every other claimant this epoch, without revealing the source. Two claims sharing one kernel are both slashed, the jury keeping a cut, so a fleet cannot hide behind one wallet. Worse, each rejected claim doubles the bond the next claim must post, a spiral making probing exponentially costly: n clones need n independent funding histories plus 2^k bonds after k failures, while one honest agent pays once.
